title: Quasi-excellence descends through finite surjective affine maps
statement: Let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$ there is a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset B$ with $f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$. If $B$ is quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring], then $A$ is quasi-excellent.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1 Step 1 (1-3), printed p.8, invocation of Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Theorem 3.1; the finite-surjective descent statement, not descent of excellence.

proof.text: By [def-exc-excellent-ring], $B$ is a G-ring and is J-2. Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, put $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$, $\widehat R$ its maximal-ideal completion, $C=R\otimes_AB$ and $D=\widehat R\otimes_AB$. Localization and completion are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian, lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. If $b_1,\ldots,b_t$ generate $B$ as an $A$-module, their images $1\otimes b_i$ generate $C$ over $R$ and $D$ over $\widehat R$: expand each tensor using $b=\sum a_i b_i$. A module generating list also generates the algebra. Thus $C,D$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. The map $R\to\widehat R$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat].

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Mathematical Journal 60 (1976), 139–149, DOI 10.1017/S0027763000017190
source.place: Greco Proposition 1.3 (ii) implies (i), and Theorem 3.1(i), printed pp.140,143; explicit finite-completion decomposition from Stacks Tag 07N9.

proof.text: The map $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is surjective: it is the base change of the assumed surjective map $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension] there is a compatible $C$-algebra identification $D\cong\prod_{\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak p}\widehat{B_{\mathfrak q}}$, with finitely many factors. On the $\mathfrak q$ factor, $C\to D$ is the map through $B_{\mathfrak q}\to\widehat{B_{\mathfrak q}}$. This last map is regular because $B$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. To check $C\to D$ is regular use [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal]. A prime of the finite product selects exactly one factor, since its prime quotient sends exactly one of the orthogonal idempotents summing to $1$ to $1$. Its local ring is the localization of that factor. If its contraction to $C$ is $\mathfrak r$, then $(B_{\mathfrak q})_{\mathfrak r B_{\mathfrak q}}=C_{\mathfrak r}$ by the universal property of localization. Consequently its local map is a localization of $B_{\mathfrak q}\to\widehat{B_{\mathfrak q}}$, regular by the same cited local criterion. That criterion gives regularity of $C\to D$.

proof.text: The canonical tensor associativity identification $\widehat R\otimes_R C\cong D$ sends $h\otimes(r\otimes b)$ to $hr\otimes b$, with inverse $h\otimes b\mapsto h\otimes(1\otimes b)$. Thus the regular map $C\to D$ is precisely the base change of the flat map $R\to\widehat R$. Apply [lem-per-regular-map-finite-surjective-detection] with source ring $R$ and finite covering algebra $C$. Its Noetherian, finite-module and spectrum-surjectivity assumptions were checked above. It follows that $A_{\mathfrak p}\to\widehat{A_{\mathfrak p}}$ is regular. Since $\mathfrak p$ was arbitrary and $A$ is Noetherian, [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] says that $A$ is a G-ring.

proof.text: For the J-2 assertion let $T$ be any commutative $A$-algebra finite as an $A$-module and let $\mathfrak t$ be a prime of $T$. Set $E=B\otimes_AT$. This is finite as a $B$-module and as a $T$-module, using tensor images of finite generating lists for $T/A$ and $B/A$, respectively. The map $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}T$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], so choose a prime $\mathfrak e$ contracting to $\mathfrak t$. Put $F=E/\mathfrak e$. The map $T/\mathfrak t\to F$ is injective, since its kernel consists exactly of classes whose representatives map into $\mathfrak e$. Both rings are domains; $F$ is finite type over $T/\mathfrak t$ and over $B$ by the displayed generating lists followed by quotient. All these rings are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Since $B$ is J-2, the regular locus of $F$ is open [def-exc-excellent-ring]. It is nonempty: at the zero prime the localization is its fraction field, of dimension zero with maximal ideal generated by the empty list [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Now [lem-exc-j0-finite-type-domain-descent] applied to $T/\mathfrak t\hookrightarrow F$ gives a nonempty open regular subset of $\operatorname{Spec}(T/\mathfrak t)$.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be a prime and $L/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ a finite purely inseparable extension, with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ the fraction field of the domain $A/\mathfrak p$. Choose a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-basis $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ of $L$ and, for each $j$, a monic $P_j=x^{m_j}+c_{j,1}x^{m_j-1}+\cdots+c_{j,m_j}\in\kappa(\mathfrak p)[x]$, $m_j\ge1$, with $P_j(y_j)=0$. Choose a nonzero $d\in A/\mathfrak p$ with $dc_{j,i}\in A/\mathfrak p$ for all $j,i$ (a product of denominators). Multiplying $P_j(y_j)=0$ by $d^{m_j}$ gives $(dy_j)^{m_j}+\sum_{i=1}^{m_j}d^{i}c_{j,i}(dy_j)^{m_j-i}=0$, a monic equation with coefficients $d^{i-1}(dc_{j,i})\in A/\mathfrak p$. Put $T=(A/\mathfrak p)[dy_1,\ldots,dy_n]\subseteq L$. By these equations every monomial in the $dy_j$ is an $A/\mathfrak p$-combination of the finitely many monomials whose exponent of $dy_j$ is below $m_j$, so $T$ is an $A$-subalgebra of $L$ finite as an $A$-module, and a domain. Its fractions exhaust $L$: if $\ell=\sum_j(a_j/s)y_j$ with $a_j,s\in A/\mathfrak p$, $s\ne0$, then $\ell=(\sum_ja_j\,dy_j)/(ds)$. Step 4 applied to this $T$ and its zero prime $\mathfrak t=0$ (so $T/\mathfrak t=T$) gives a nonempty open subset of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ at whose points $T$ is regular local. These are the hypotheses of [lem-exc-j2-residue-field-criterion], so $A$ is J-2. We have proved that $A$ is Noetherian, a G-ring and J-2, hence quasi-excellent by [def-exc-excellent-ring].
